chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Muhammad ibn Isa from Sulayman ibn Hafsh al-Marwazi said:

The Jurist (peace be upon him) said: 'The sick person only prays sitting if he reaches a state in which he cannot walk the distance equivalent to the duration of his prayer while standing until he finishes.'
And whoever is in a state of illness that necessitates breaking the fast, and he strives to fast, it does not suffice for him, and he must make up for it.
This is indicated by the saying of the Exalted: 'And whoever is sick or on a journey, then an equal number of other days.'
Thus, He obligated upon the sick person, by the apparent meaning of the wording, an equal number of other days.

key_terms.عِدَّةٌ مِنْ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَ: An equal number of other days

ai.seo_question: What is the condition under which a sick person is required to pray while sitting rather than standing?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling in the chapter defining the threshold of illness that necessitates breaking fast, establishing that sitting in prayer is permitted only when standing becomes physically impossible for the duration of the prayer. The hadith further clarifies that voluntarily fasting while ill invalidates the obligation, requiring later makeup (qada), a principle derived directly from the explicit wording of the Quranic verse regarding travelers and the sick.
